selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: Random-walk-based Probabilistic Microglia Morphology Reconstruction in 2D and 3D from Confocal Microscopy Images
papers.authors: Chen, X.; Hossain, E.; McCall, M. N.
papers.abstract: Reconstructing individual microglia from confocal images is challenging when fine processes have weak fluorescence or neighboring cells form connected structures. Inspired by Grady's random-walker framework, we propose a soma-guided probabilistic method for three-dimensional microglial reconstruction and cell-of-origin assignment. Signal-weighted random walks quantify voxel connectivity to each soma by the probability of reaching that soma before background or another soma. A path-length adjustment reduces the penalty on distal processes. Adjusted scores are compared across somata to assign voxels, subject to score and image-intensity thresholds. We assess process recovery and cell assignment separately using exact three-dimensional matching to manual tracings. In a P28 single-cell example, the reconstruction covered 83.98% of traced voxels within the analyzed region. For a connected cell pair in sample 12hrMD82, coverage was 71.86% and 82.31%, with a pooled incorrect-assignment rate of 4.61% among detected traced voxels. Local analyses were also combined to produce an overview of 13 cell reconstructions in the same sample. We additionally provide a two-dimensional version that tolerates short signal gaps in maximum-intensity projections. These initial examples demonstrate the potential of soma-specific connectivity for microglial reconstruction.

papers.title: IGH and IGK Next-Generation Sequencing Testing in Multiple Myeloma: A Comparison of CD138-Positive Sorted and Unsorted Bone Marrow Samples.
papers.authors: Choi YJ, Park YJ, Choi J, Lee ST, Choi JR, Shin S.
papers.abstract: Identifying a patient-specific immunoglobulin (Ig) gene clonotype at diagnosis is a prerequisite for next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based measurable residual disease monitoring in multiple myeloma but may fail in low-tumor-burden samples. We evaluated the effect of CD138-positive plasma cell enrichment on Ig heavy chain ( IGH ) and Ig kappa ( IGK ) NGS clonotype detection in a paired split-sample cohort (N=20) and an unpaired cohort (N=60) tested before and after routine implementation of enrichment. In the paired cohort, enrichment numerically increased IGH detection from 65.0% to 85.0% and IGK detection from 65.0% to 80.0%. All 15 patients positive in both aliquots shared at least one exact sequence-matched clonotype. For dominant matched clonotypes, the clonal read fraction increased for IGH (median, 27.8% to 85.2%; P =0.0105) but not for IGK (33.6% to 36.9%; P =0.0942). In the unpaired cohort, overall detection in specimens with P =0.021; exploratory). Thus, CD138-positive plasma cell enrichment may increase NGS-based clonotype detection, although paired detection-rate differences were not statistically significant. Prospective paired validation, particularly in low-burden specimens, is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

papers.title: Transcriptomic-Methylation Integration and Machine-Learning Prioritization of Candidate Prognostic Biomarkers in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Computational Study
papers.authors: MANNEKUNTA, N.; NATRAJAN, E.
papers.abstract: Background: Triple-negative breast cancer is molecularly heterogeneous, complicating prognostic stratification. We aimed to derive a gene panel and clinical-genomic survival nomogram and assess cross-platform performance. Methods: This retrospective computational study analyzed The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer data, identifying 197 primary-tumor transcriptomic aliquots from 190 patients. Differential gene-expression and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation analyses comparing Dead versus Alive vital status were performed separately. Candidate lists meeting nominal significance (p < 0.05) were intersected by gene symbol to identify a 47-gene discovery signature. Random Forest feature importance, corroborated by LightGBM, prioritized 15 genes. Among 190 patients (163 alive, 27 deceased), standardization and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique resampling yielded 326 observations before an 80%/20% split. Seven classifiers were evaluated; a five-fold sigmoid-calibrated soft-voting ensemble generated the 15-gene risk score. Prognostic performance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a clinical-genomic nomogram. Six immune-infiltration profiles and three immune-checkpoint genes were compared between risk groups. External validation used the GSE58812 microarray cohort (n = 107). Results: Multi-omic integration yielded a 47-gene signature and 15-gene panel. In the 47-gene resampled test partition (n = 66), LightGBM achieved 95.45% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9899; Support Vector Machine achieved the highest AUC (0.9935). Risk groups differed in overall survival (log-rank p < 0.0001). The risk score remained associated with survival after adjustment for age and advanced stage (hazard ratio 10.67 per standard-deviation increase; 95% confidence interval 6.64-17.15; p < 0.001). Time-dependent AUCs were 0.910, 0.911, and 0.937 at 1, 3, and 5 years. The nomogram estimated 3- and 5-year survival probabilities. Immune-profile (p = 0.38-0.93) and checkpoint-gene differences (p = 0.50-0.74) were not significant. Untouched independent external validation in GSE58812 yielded fixed-model AUCs of 0.4191-0.5500; post-validation XGBoost optimization yielded a gene-only AUC of 0.5533, while an exploratory risk-plus-age score yielded 0.6874. Conclusions: The 15-gene signature showed prognostic association and potentially optimistic internal performance; the nomogram provided a framework for individualized survival estimation. Independent external validation showed limited gene-only transferability; optimized and age-integrated results remain exploratory and require independent assessment.

papers.title: Single-cell T cell receptor sequencing deciphers αβ- and γδ-T cell responses in neuroblastoma
papers.authors: Zappa, E.; Hiddink Verberne, N.; Messing, S. A.; Purayamkott Murikkumchery, F.; Sanchez Sanchez, G.; Almeida Andrezo, S.; De Munter, S.; Vandekerckhove, B.; Tan, C. L.; Balwierz, A. K.; de Jonge, W. J.; DeMartino, J.; Lijnzaad, P.; Margaritis, T.; Borst, A. A.; van der Steeg, A. F. W.; de Krijger, R.; Dierselhuis, M. P.; Tytgat, G. A. M.; Wolkers, M.; Green, E. W.; Scheper, W.; Vermijlen, D.; Molenaar, J. J.; Wienke, J.
papers.abstract: High-risk neuroblastoma is a pediatric tumor with poor survival rates and low MHC-I expression. The cellular determinants of anti-tumor immunity remain poorly defined, limiting development of targeted immunotherapies. We generated a single-cell atlas integrating transcriptomic and {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing of >150,000 T cells from tumor and blood of 10 patients throughout treatment. Fractions of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells are clonally expanded and activated, with tumor-specific expansion among CD4+ cells. Transcriptomic evidence of tumor-reactivity is more pronounced in CD4+ than CD8+ T cells. Moreover, V{delta}1+ {gamma}{delta}T cells are enriched, displaying TCR engagement. Functional screening confirmed reactivity of selected {gamma}{delta}TCRs and, remarkably, a small fraction of CD8+ {beta}TCRs. Subset-specific inhibitory receptors, including CTLA4, FCRL6, and KIRs, may serve as targets for tailored immunotherapies. Together, we identify distinct {beta}- and {gamma}{delta}T cell responses despite low MHC-I, and provide a comprehensive resource for deciphering pediatric immunity against MHC-Ilow tumors.

papers.title: A Molecular Review of the T-Cell Receptor: CD3 Molecule Structure, Activation Pathways, and Clustering.
papers.authors: Buttigieg JP, Bright R.
papers.abstract: The T-cell receptor (TCR)-CD3 complex couples antigen recognition to intracellular signalling and is central to adaptive immunity. However, how ligand-binding kinetics, mechanical forces and membrane organization collectively regulate TCR activation remains incompletely understood. Here, we critically evaluate competing models of TCR activation and discuss how receptor dwell time, membrane organization, and signalling microdomains govern TCR activation. We propose an integrative conceptual framework, termed the spatiotemporal kinetic integration model, in which TCR signalling emerges from the combined effects of ligand dwell time, membrane organization and CD3 phosphorylation dynamics. This review explains how the TCR heterodimer (αβ or γδ) links with CD3γε, CD3δε, and CD3ζζ dimers. It highlights how immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs (ITAMs) govern signal transduction. We explore key early signalling pathways, including Lck-driven phosphorylation, ZAP-70 recruitment, and activation of phospholipase C-γ1 (PLC-γ1), which leads to calcium release and gene activation. Additionally, we review new evidence on TCR clustering and membrane behaviour, considering how receptor movement (i.e., TCRs moving around a T cell) can affect interpretations of TCR arrangement. We discuss recent progress in high-resolution imaging and single-molecule methods and consider key challenges and future directions for studying T-cell activation at both the molecular and single-cell levels. A clearer understanding of these mechanisms will help explain how T cells integrate biochemical and mechanical information across spatial and temporal scales.

papers.title: SingloCell: an open and accessible web platform for multimodal single-cell data exploration
papers.authors: Allot, A.; Wu, H.; Afanasiev, E.; Yaqubi, M.; Recinto, S. J.; Oram, C.; Farimani, S.; Zhang, Y.; Creeggan, F.; Gertsvolf, J.; Ragoussis, J.; Nagy, C.; Ding, J.; Farhan, S. M. K.; Poulin, J.-F.; Stratton, J. A.
papers.abstract: Single-cell research is transforming biology and medicine, offering unprecedented insight into health and disease. Yet, the true potential of single-cell data can only be realized when datasets are open, easy to interact with, and accessible to all. We introduce SingloCell (https://singlocell.openscience.mcgill.ca/), an intuitive multimodal single-cell web platform built on three principles: accessibility, interactivity and traceability. SingloCell provides free browser-based access to single-cell datasets and supports user submission of suspension-based transcriptomics, proteomics, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-derived gene activity matrices), immune receptor (BCR, TCR) and multi-omics modalities, as well as spatial datasets. This enables researchers, clinicians, educators, and the broader community to explore high-dimensional datasets without programming expertise. Users can explore and analyse data in real time using tools for differential gene expression, functional enrichment, and pathway visualisation, while also examining pre-computed analyses such as pseudotime trajectories and cell-cell interactions. Datasets can be shared publicly or via unlisted links, and analytical workflows are documented through downloadable receipts.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics and in vitro validation reveal MIF as a promoter of breast cancer progression in an immune-related context.
papers.authors: Chen B, Liu Y, Zhang W, Yang S, Wei L, Wei C, Tan Q.
papers.abstract: The molecular pathogenesis of breast cancer (BC) is exceedingly complex and centrally involves immune-related genes (IRGs) yet the direct genetic contributions of many such genes to the disease are not fully understood. This investigation therefore utilized a multi-omics strategy to establish the Genetic association of pivotal IRGs in BC and validate their clinical significance. Publicly available genetic, transcriptomic, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) date were analyzed to identify IRGs associated with BC. Differentially expressed genes were intersected with IRGs, and Genetically inferred causal associations were evaluated using two-sample MR. Candidate genes were validated by bioinformatics analyses, RT-qPCR, and IHC. Functional enrichment, drug sensitivity prediction, and scRNA-seq analyses further elucidated their biological significance. We identified 309 candidate IRGs associated with BC. MR analysis established a Genetically inferred causal association for 8 of these genes. Among them, IL21R, TLR4, MIF, IL17D, and OLR1 showed consistent differential expression and were designated as key genes. Crucially, experimental validation confirmed these findings; in both breast cancer cell lines and clinical tumor tissues, IL21R, MIF, and OLR1 were significantly upregulated, whereas TLR4 and IL17D were downregulated compared to non-malignant controls. Functional analysis revealed a pronounced enrichment of these genes within pivotal biological networks and bioinformatic prediction suggested their association with the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. Subsequent in vitro functional validation demonstrated that MIF silencing significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of MDA-MB-231 BC cells, while recombinant MIF supplementation restored these malignant phenotypes. All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) treatment reduced MIF and OLR1 mRNA expression, increased IL17D mRNA expression, and inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion in MDA-MB-231 cells. Our study identified IL21R, TLR4, MIF, IL17D, and OLR1 as key IRGs associated with BC and experimentally supported a role for MIF in promoting malignant phenotypes. Preliminary ATRA validation demonstrated changes in selected IRG expression and inhibition of malignant phenotypes. These findings provide insights into the immune-related molecular features of BC and potential avenues for therapeutic exploration.

papers.title: Single‑Cell Transcriptomic Reanalysis Reveals Neuronal Transcriptional States and Neuro‑Immune Remodeling After Peripheral Nerve Injury.
papers.authors: Fu D, Adili A, Chen X, Li J, Li, Maimaitiabudula A, Muheremu A.
papers.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) causes severe sensorimotor deficits and neuropathic pain, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) remain incompletely understood. In this study, we aimed to identify the transcriptional states of specific neuronal subtypes after PNI and to characterize potentially associated neuro-immune remodeling. We reanalyzed a public scRNA-seq dataset (GSE255014) from mouse L4-L5 DRG at day 3 after chronic constriction injury (CCI). Neuronal subtype-associated transcriptional states, macrophage heterogeneity, and predicted ligand-receptor interactions were systematically analyzed using unbiased clustering, differential expression, AUCell, SCENIC, pseudotime trajectory inference, and CellChat. PNI was associated with cell type proportion imbalance and apoptosis pathway activation. Among nine confirmed neuronal subtypes, the recovered Nefm⁺ neurofilament-containing neuronal subpopulation showed an apparent reduction after CCI, accompanied by expansion of a Sprr1a⁺ regeneration-associated neurons. Moreover, Atf3 and Jun were significantly upregulated in Nefm⁺ neurons and may serve as candidate key regulators cooperatively driving the transition of this subtype toward an injury/regeneration-associated state. In macrophages, six subpopulations with distinct transcriptomic profiles were identified. The dominant resident-like Cd163⁺ subpopulation decreased noticeably after CCI, whereas the Ccr2⁺ pro-inflammatory subpopulation expanded markedly. Pseudotime ordering revealed a transcriptional continuum from resident‑like to pro-inflammatory states. Cell-cell communication analysis showed that incoming signaling to Ccr2⁺ macrophages was considerably enhanced during PNI. Notably, App-Cd74 signaling axes was weakened between Nefm⁺ neurons and Cd163⁺ macrophages but enhanced between Nefm⁺ neurons and Ccr2⁺ macrophages, which may specifically promote local infiltration and pro-inflammatory activation of Ccr2⁺ macrophages. Our study indicates that day 3 post-CCI induced marked transcriptional remodeling of Nefm+ neurons in the DRG and highlighted abnormal crosstalk between these neurons and macrophages. These findings deepen our understanding of the neuroimmune pathogenic mechanisms in the early stage of PNI and may therefore inform future improved therapeutic strategies for neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning-assisted SOM-PMF cross-corroboration and source-oriented risk assessment of soil heavy metals at an industrial site in the Yangtze River Delta.
papers.authors: Han Z, Wang Y, He L, Shi J, Luo J, Cao W, Zou Q.
papers.abstract: Industrial-site soil heavy metal contamination is spatially heterogeneous and source-complex, challenging safe redevelopment and precise risk management. At a typical industrial site in the Yangtze River Delta, contamination, sources, and risks of heavy metals were assessed, with emphasis on Pb and Cd. A combined HCA-SOM-PMF framework was used for source apportionment, with a novel RF-SHAP-assisted analysis of SOM cluster signatures supporting quantitative cross-corroboration with PMF. MCS supported depth-specific probabilistic risk assessment, and PMF contributions were coupled with risk models to quantify source-specific risks. Pb and Cd contamination levels decreased markedly with depth, with high contamination levels mainly concentrated in the upper 0-1.0 m. PMF identified natural, industrial mixed, mechanical processing, and welding and coating sources. RF-SHAP suggested Cd, Pb, and Hg as potential discriminating metals in Clusters Ⅱ and Ⅲ. SOM clusters showed some agreement with dominant PMF factors (ARI = 0.543), but mixed factor contributions within clusters (N eff = 1.69-2.07) indicated no strict one-to-one correspondence. Risk assessment indicated very high ecological risk in the upper 0-1.0 m and a potential non-carcinogenic risk for children. Despite contributing only 2.9% of the total heavy metal mass, the mechanical processing source accounted for 94.6% of RI and 66.8% and 68.0% of TCR for children and adults, respectively. The industrial mixed source dominated non-carcinogenic risk, contributing 60.6% and 59.2% of HI. By combining interpretable SOM-PMF cross-corroboration with source-oriented risk assessment, this study strengthens source interpretation and supports risk-based remediation priorities.

papers.title: Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease: from glial heterogeneity and gut-brain immune crosstalk to precision therapeutic strategies.
papers.authors: Wei Y, Fu K, Gong L, Ma Q, Xu P, Li R.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, α-synuclein pathology, and a broad spectrum of motor and non-motor manifestations. Neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as an important component of PD pathobiology; however, traditional frameworks have largely focused on canonical inflammatory pathways and simplified classifications of glial activation, which do not fully capture the spatial, temporal, and functional heterogeneity of immune responses in PD. Emerging evidence from single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, together with studies of peripheral immunity and the microbiota-gut-brain axis, indicates that PD-associated inflammation is dynamic, context dependent, and systemically integrated. In this review, we critically synthesize current evidence on microglial and astrocytic activation, bidirectional glial crosstalk, α-synuclein-inflammation feedback loops, and the selective vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons. We further discuss region- and disease-stage-dependent glial states, systemic immune and gut-brain interactions, and inflammation-associated microRNAs as potential links between peripheral and central inflammatory responses. Therapeutically, we evaluate conventional anti-inflammatory strategies alongside emerging RNA-based interventions and targeted delivery approaches. Particular attention is given to the persistent translational gap between robust preclinical efficacy and limited disease-modifying benefit in patients, including limitations related to disease models, therapeutic timing, biomarker availability, patient heterogeneity, and blood-brain barrier penetration. Collectively, current evidence supports a shift from broad suppression of inflammation toward biomarker-guided, disease-stage-specific, and cell- or pathway-selective immunomodulation in PD.

papers.title: Mechanical Checkpoints in Antitumor Immunity: From Piezo1 to AFM Nanomechanics.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Yin X, Deng Q, Ju T, Wang Z.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy resistance in solid tumors remains a major clinical challenge. One emerging reason is that the tumor microenvironment exhibits aberrant mechanical properties-tissues become stiff, and cancer cells become soft. These mechanical changes directly affect how T cells migrate, form synapses, and kill target cells. In this review, we first describe how the extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening and cancer cell softening create a physical barrier that limits immune cell function. We then focus on Piezo1, a mechanosensitive ion channel that acts as a "mechanical checkpoint" in T cells. Acute mechanical stimulation activates Piezo1 and enhances T cell cytotoxicity, while chronic overstimulation in a stiff tumor environment drives T cell exhaustion through the CaMKII-CREB-Osr2 pathway. Next, we show how atomic force microscopy (AFM) can measure single-cell mechanics, track real-time mechanical death trajectories during immune attack, and help identify mechano-biomarkers. Finally, we discuss strategies to target these mechanical pathways, including Piezo1 agonists/antagonists, "mechanical biopsy," and physical interventions such as focused ultrasound. We also point out current problems, including the lack of standardized methods, tumor heterogeneity, and limited clinical translation. Nevertheless, integrating mechano-immunology into cancer therapy does not replace traditional immunotherapy but expands it. By correcting mechanical abnormalities and using AFM-based characterization, we may improve the effectiveness of immunotherapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: Longitudinal multiomics analysis in blood from individuals before and after HIV acquisition
papers.authors: Moron-Lopez, S.; Garrido-Sanz, L.; Soriaga, L.; Urrea, V.; Wong, E.; Dalmau, J.; Gomez-Gomez, A.; Haro, N.; Coll, P.; Mothe, B.; Ruiz-Riol, M.; Pozo, O. J.; Clotet, B.; Brander, C.; Telenti, A.; Martinez-Picado, J.
papers.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of cellular immunity is essential for controlling viral infections, yet individual and coordinated immune responses continue to pose significant challenges in HIV cure research. Recent advances in single-cell and multiomics technologies provide powerful tools to dissect intricate multicellular behaviors and identify novel therapeutic targets. Direct characterization of HIV-induced immune alterations is challenging because matched samples obtained before HIV acquisition are rare. To better understand individual and coordinated cellular immune responses relevant to HIV cure research, we integrated single-nucleus chromatin-accessibility and transcriptomic profiling of 150,060 PBMCs with plasma metabolome, lipidome and soluble immune-profiling from five individuals before HIV acquisition, during early infection and after at least six months of suppressive antiretroviral therapy (ART). HIV acquisition expanded activated CD8 T and proliferating NK/CD8 T cells and induced cell-type-specific chromatin and transcriptional changes enriched for interferon, inflammatory and TNF-NF-{kappa}B programs, many persisting during ART. Multiome sequencing detected 32 HIV-positive cells which were associated with increased expression of IFI44L during early infection and ATAD3A after ART. Plasma IP-10 increased transiently, whereas eight energy- or amino-acid-related metabolites showed nominal decreases persisting after ART. These paired observations distinguish transient inflammatory responses from persistent molecular and metabolic perturbations after HIV acquisition.

papers.title: Interpretable Blood Transcriptomic Classification of Ebola Survivors: A Machine Learning Framework for Post-Recovery Immune Profiling.
papers.authors: Bantun F, Aldairi AF, Faidah H, Babalghith AO, Johargy AK, Ahmad F, Mathkor DM, Haque S, Srivastava V.
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors may experience persistent immune dysfunction and inflammatory complications after recovery, highlighting the need for blood-based approaches to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. We investigated whether whole-blood transcriptomics could distinguish EVD survivors (EVD-Ss) from healthy controls and identify candidate transcriptional features associated with survivor status. Public whole-blood RNA-sequencing data from 26 EVD-Ss and 33 healthy donors from the same geographical region in Guinea [Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO): GSE143549] were analyzed using DESeq2 for differential expression. An elastic-net logistic regression classifier underwent nested cross-validation (5 outer, 3 inner folds), with gene ranking, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning restricted exclusively to training splits. Performance was assessed using 100 repeated partitions and a full-pipeline permutation test (1,000 permutations). Gene-selection stability was evaluated across 500 cross-validation fits and 200 subsamples, with comparisons against principal-component-only, cell-composition-only, and sex-only models. The classifier achieved a pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.962 [95% DeLong confidence interval (CI): 0.917 to 1.000] and mean repeated-cross-validation AUC of 0.960 (95% subject-bootstrap CI: 0.926 to 0.987). Gene selection varied from 1 to 50 genes across resampled fits; a principal-component-only model showed comparable discrimination. Candidate genes require further validation of reproducibility and biological relevance and represent an exploratory, unstable set rather than a validated signature. These findings identify a whole-blood transcriptional signal associated with EVD-S status, supporting further investigation of transcriptomic profiling to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. Independent validation and linkage with immune functions and clinical outcomes are required before its effectiveness for routine clinical survivor monitoring can be reliably assessed.

papers.title: RNA-defined R-loop-associated malignant-cell states are accompanied by chromatin and antigen-presentation remodeling in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Liu Q, Ding T, Liu W, Han B, Liu D, Zhang W, Wu J, Xu H, Zhao E, Li X, Wang J, You B, Nan Y.
papers.abstract: Background RNA-defined R-loop-associated malignant-cell states and their chromatin correlates in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain incompletely characterized. Methods We integrated GSE207493 and GSE264586 single-cell RNA-sequencing data and calculated a frozen 18-gene R-loop-associated score from raw counts after CPM normalization and log2(CPM+1) transformation. Patient-level models assessed transcriptional associations, while patient-matched scATAC-seq was analyzed using pseudobulk, chromVAR and RNA-ATAC concordance analyses. Dataset-specific and pooled scTenifoldKnk models prioritized NCL for cellular validation. Results Twelve of 25 prespecified transcriptional programs were associated with the continuous patient-level score at BH q Conclusions The RNA-derived score defines a ccRCC malignant-cell state with coordinated transcriptional and chromatin-accessibility remodeling. NCL perturbation and RNase H1 intervention support an NCL-dependent, RNase H-sensitive link to DNA damage and antigen-presentation/checkpoint remodeling.

papers.title: Spatial organization of immunosuppressive niches is associated with immune exclusion in ETMR.
papers.authors: Cao Y, Reyes-González JM, Okada R, Oh J, Syed N, Biswas S, Wang B, Nellan A, Cotter J, Ruppin E, Nguyen R.
papers.abstract: Background Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare and highly aggressive malignant pediatric brain tumor with limited treatments. The spatial organization of the ETMR immune microenvironment remains poorly understood, limiting our understanding of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance. Methods We defined the spatial organization of ETMR using spatial transcriptomics across 11 samples from 9 patients, integrated with independent publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Results Immune cells were largely excluded from the tumor core, while the peritumoral border formed an immunosuppressive niche enriched for B-cells and M2-like macrophages. These cells exhibited conserved transcriptional programs associated with gliosis, extracellular matrix generation, immune suppression, and cellular exhaustion. At this interface, the CD74-MIF signaling axis was enriched, suggesting a possible coordinated mechanism underlying peritumoral macrophage and regulatory B-cell abundance. Integration with the ETMR developmental continuum further revealed spatial covariation between tumor developmental states and immune and stromal features. Multilayered rosettes, a histopathological hallmark of ETMR, showed spatially confined interferon-responsive, immune-associated transcriptional programs, enriched for type I and II interferon signaling and antigen-processing pathways. This suggests that despite global immune exclusion, localized regions of interferon-responsive and immune-associated transcriptional activity persist within the tumor. Conclusion These findings define a compartmentalized spatial immune architecture in ETMR characterized by relative immune depletion in tumor-rich regions, immunoregulatory and stroma-associated programs at selected tumor interfaces, and localized interferon-responsive transcriptional activity within rosette-associated regions. This spatial framework provides a basis for future mechanistic studies of tumor-immune interactions and their potential therapeutic relevance in ETMR.

papers.title: A Spatial and Single-Cell Atlas of Early Human Alveolar Bone Healing.
papers.authors: Li A, Chen H, Zhou J, Xu S, Du M, Ge S, Li P.
papers.abstract: Aim To construct an integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of early human alveolar bone healing to delineate cellular heterogeneity and intercellular communication during the proliferative phase. Methods Granulation tissue was harvested from the extraction sockets of seven healthy patients 4 weeks post extraction. Six patients provided samples for single-cell RNA sequencing and one for spatial transcriptomics. Bioinformatic analyses characterised cellular subpopulations, pseudotemporal relationships and predicted communication networks. Immunofluorescence assessed spatial proximity between fibroblast and endothelial cell populations. Results Fifteen major cell populations and two transcriptionally distinct fibroblast subsets were identified: WNT5A + fibroblasts were associated with inflammatory responses and immune cell recruitment, whereas OGN + fibroblasts were linked to extracellular matrix organisation, tissue remodelling and ossification. Macrophage, T-cell and endothelial subsets were also identified. OGN + fibroblasts showed extensive interactions with immune and endothelial subsets, including CXCL12-CXCR4. Spatial transcriptomics revealed heterogeneous distributions of major cell populations and their subsets. Immunofluorescence further indicated spatial proximity between CXCL12-expressing fibroblasts and CXCR4 + endothelial cells. Conclusions This atlas characterises cellular and spatial heterogeneity during early human alveolar bone healing and highlights fibroblast-associated interactions for future functional investigation.

papers.title: Keratinocytes as innate sensors and responders in skin homeostasis and repair.
papers.authors: Toniolo A, Hoste E.
papers.abstract: Keratinocytes serve as crucial structural cells providing epidermal barrier integrity but also orchestrate cutaneous immune signalling paramount to skin homeostasis, inflammation, repair and carcinogenesis. Keratinocytes sense the presence of microbial or damage-induced stressors and consequently secrete a vast array of cytokines and chemokines, resulting in recruitment and/or activation of immune cells. The interaction of keratinocytes with innate immune cells is designed to facilitate fast onset of inflammatory responses and constitutes a complex and multi-layered interplay. Timely resolution of these responses is important to avert inflammatory skin disease. Here, we summarise recent findings on how keratinocytes receive innate immune signals and respond to them in homeostatic and reparative conditions. Recent spatial and single-cell RNA-sequencing studies on murine and human skin provide unique insights in the cellular and molecular interplay in homeostatic and reparative skin at temporal resolution. Understanding this complex dialogue between keratinocytes and skin-resident and -recruited immune cells in reparative inflammation is instrumental to improve clinical wound care.

papers.title: Automated Standardization of Companion Diagnostics Using Deep Learning: Claudin18.2 as a Paradigm in Gastric Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang X, Zheng K, Chen J, Zheng X, Zhao Z, Hu W, Liu L, Lu S, Zhou J, Kong L, Wen X, Luo R, Zhang Y, Nie R, Yun J, Wang R, Xie D, Guo R, Cai MY.
papers.abstract: Companion diagnostic biomarkers are essential for selecting patients for targeted and immunotherapeutic intervention. However, their clinical implementation is frequently limited by analytical reproducibility, inter-observer variability, and clone-dependent interpretation in immunohistochemistry (IHC) assays. Claudin18.2, an emerging biomarker in gastric cancer, exemplifies these challenges. We developed an end-to-end, deep learning-driven pipeline augmented with active learning for automated and quantitative assessment of IHC-stained whole-slide images (WSIs). Using Claudin18.2 as a representative biomarker, the model was trained on 43-14A clone and validated in both retrospective and prospective gastric cancer cohorts. Generalizability across alternative antibody clones was assessed, and the model's capacity for cross-clone concordance analysis was investigated. The model demonstrated almost perfect agreement with the pathologist-defined reference standard for 2/3+ staining (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.849 and 0.894) and robust classification performance across clinically relevant thresholds (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.764-0.828 and 0.865-0.904), matching or surpassing pathologists' evaluation while improving efficiency. Importantly, the pipeline maintained strong performance in cross-clone analyses, supporting clone-independent application. This scalable AI framework enables standardized, quantitative, and cross-clone interpretation of Claudin18.2 IHC; the approach has the potential to enhance the precision, reproducibility, and accessibility of biomarker-driven patient selection in routine clinical practice.

papers.title: VSIG4 promotes renal cancer progression by inducing AKT-mediated epithelial-mesenchymal transition and is linked to an immunosuppressive immune microenvironment.
papers.authors: Fu Z, Jia Z, Zhang T, Lu K, Shi M, Wu J, Wang C, Zhang G, Kong Y, Huang Y.
papers.abstract: The treatment options for metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC) are limited, and treatment efficacy is poor. New treatment methods are urgently needed to improve the clinical outcomes of mccRCC patients. VSIG4 is an oncogene that is involved in the growth and migration of various tumours. However, the biological role of VSIG4 in renal cancer and the related mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the role of VSIG4 in the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer and the related molecular mechanisms. We used the CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE methods to calculate the proportion of infiltrating immune cells and the proportion of immune stroma in 551 clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. The R package "limma" was used to screen for differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Univariate Cox regression analysis and protein‒protein interaction (PPI) network analysis were employed to identify the core genes among the DEGs. Further analysis was conducted on the correlation between the expression of the core gene VSIG4 and immune cell infiltration as well as clinicopathological characteristics. The expression level of VSIG4 was measured using qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Lentiviral infection was used to downregulate VSIG4 expression in renal cancer cells. CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, scratch, and Transwell assays were performed to evaluate the biological function of VSIG4 in renal cancer cells. In vivo experiments in mice were carried out to explore the effects of VSIG4 inhibition on the proliferation and metastasis of renal cancer cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that VSIG4 was highly expressed in ccRCC and that its expression level was positively correlated with tumour stage and grade. VSIG4 is a key molecule that promotes the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer. The results of patient sample verification indicated that the expression of VSIG4 in renal cancer tissues was significantly greater than that in adjacent normal tissues. Downregulation of VSIG4 inactivated the p-AKT signaling pathway, consequently impairing epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and associated migratory capacity. Moreover, it was closely related to the inhibition of PD-L1 and IL-10 and the activation of IL-2, IL-4, IFN-γ, and SHP-2 (PTPN11). VSIG4 is highly expressed in renal cancer tissues and promotes the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer cells. This effect is mediated, at least in part, through the AKT signaling pathway, which concurrently drives EMT, upregulates PD‑L1 and IL‑10, and downregulates IL‑2, IL‑4, IFN‑γ, and SHP‑2 (PTPN11).Our results collectively establish VSIG4 as a promising therapeutic target of renal cancer progression and validate its potential as a therapeutic target for ccRCC intervention.

papers.title: Prioritization of Candidate Genes and Predicted Compounds for Presbycusis by Mendelian Randomization With Multidimensional Bioinformatics Analysis.
papers.authors: Yu S, Yu H, Wang W, Wang F, Wang X, Banerjee S.
papers.abstract: To prioritize candidate genes and computationally predicted compounds for presbycusis, we integrated an exploratory expression screen with two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) using whole-blood eQTL data from the eQTLGen Consortium and presbycusis GWAS data from the EBI database. Functional-enrichment, immune-cell-infiltration, pathway, motif, regulatory-network, and compound-perturbation analyses were performed for biological interpretation. Among 145-gene expression-presbycusis associations evaluated by primary MR, nine associations supported by at least three instrumental SNPs met the nominal IVW threshold of p 0.70 and were selected for exploratory downstream characterization. Immune-infiltration analysis showed higher neutrophil and eosinophil proportions and lower mast-cell and activated dendritic-cell proportions in the older group. GSVA linked GLIPR2 and COL9A2 mainly to WNT/ β -catenin signaling and ESPN and DPP4 to apical-surface signaling. Motif analysis identified cisbp_M6547 as the most enriched motif (NES = 5.31), with predicted enrichment for COL9A2 and ESPN. Expression analysis identified strong correlations between GLIPR2 and CYBA and between ESPN and ACTG1, and a predicted network comprising four mRNAs and 27 miRNAs was constructed. CMap analysis prioritized azacitidine, dilazep, GSK-3 inhibitor II, ivermectin, and sunitinib as compounds with expression profiles inversely correlated with the presbycusis-associated signature. These findings provide genetically informed candidates and testable hypotheses that require independent replication and experimental validation.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis of the potential mechanism of morin against myocardial infarction.
papers.authors: Wei F, Tian M.
papers.abstract: Background As a typical natural flavonoid compound, morin exerts definite cardioprotective effects. Nevertheless, its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms in the treatment of myocardial infarction have not been fully elucidated. Methods This study combined network pharmacology and bioinformatic strategies to screen candidate targets of morin as well as genes closely associated with myocardial infarction across diverse databases. Further validations were implemented via functional enrichment analysis, three machine learning models including LASSO regression, SVM-RFE and random forest algorithm, immune infiltration assessment and molecular docking verification. Results Through a multi-step screening process, six candidate genes were identified, including ARG1, CDK6, CXCR1, CYP1B1, MMP9, and PFKFB3. These candidate genes are enriched in inflammation- and metabolism-related signaling pathways, including the TNF, AMPK, HIF-1, and IL-17 pathways, as well as pathways involved in arachidonic acid metabolism and phagocytosis. Immune association analysis suggests that these genes are associated with neutrophils, macrophages, and mast cells. Molecular docking simulations predict a potential binding interaction between mulberry pigment and these target proteins. Conclusions Morin may alleviate damage caused by myocardial infarction by regulating immune and inflammatory responses, metabolic processes, and tissue remodeling.

papers.title: Beyond Amyloid in Alzheimer's Disease: A Multiscale Evidence-Based Review of Pathogenesis, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapeutics.
papers.authors: Gupta R, Lakhanpal S, Gupta S, Rawat JM, Ravi K, Abomughaid MM, Jha NK, Singh KK, Kumar N.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterised neuropathologically by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, phosphorylated-tau neurofibrillary tangles, synaptic dysfunction, and neuronal loss. However, the temporal and causal relationships underlying disease initiation, progression, and clinical heterogeneity remain incompletely resolved. Increasing evidence supports a multiscale model in which amyloid-tau pathology intersects with genetic susceptibility, epigenetic regulation, impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial and metabolic stress, neuroimmune activation, vascular dysfunction, and declining neural resilience. Familial variants in APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 directly perturb amyloid processing, whereas APOE ε4, TREM2, and polygenic variation influence lipid metabolism, protein clearance, vascular integrity, and glial responses. DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, and non-coding RNAs may further shape neuronal and immune states, although their directionality and causal significance remain incompletely established. Similarly, microbial and environmental exposures have been associated with inflammatory and proteostatic alterations, but definitive evidence for causation in sporadic AD is lacking. This review integrates genetic, epigenetic, proteostatic, metabolic, neuroimmune, vascular, and environmental mechanisms across disease stages and cellular compartments. We critically evaluate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma biomarkers, amyloid/tau PET, multimodal imaging, extracellular vesicles, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, stratification, and therapeutic prioritisation. Therapeutic evidence is stratified from established symptomatic treatments and approved anti-amyloid antibodies to investigational tau-, immune-, epigenetic-, RNA-, microbiome-, stem-cell-, neuromodulatory-, and nanoparticle-based strategies. By distinguishing causal human evidence from observational, experimental, and computational findings, this synthesis identifies priorities for biomarker-guided, stage-specific, and mechanism-informed interventions while avoiding premature inference of causality or clinical benefit.
papers.venue: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine

papers.title: Association of sleep patterns with organ aging: a large community-based study.
papers.authors: Miao Y, Li X, Dai S, Dove A, Arvanitakis Z, Xu W, Zhang Q.
papers.abstract: Sleep plays an essential role in biological processes, but its relationship with biological aging is under-explored. We examined the relationship between sleep patterns and both organ age gaps and accelerated organ aging. This study included 247,697 participants without major chronic disease, from the UK Biobank (mean age: 55.20 ± 8.09). Eight organ system-specific ages (cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain) were constructed using machine learning, incorporating biomarker, physiological, anthropometric, and neuroimaging data. Organ-specific age gaps (the difference between estimated age and chronological age) were calculated, and accelerated organ aging was defined as an organ age gap exceeding the 95th percentile. Sleep patterns were self-reported at baseline, comprising sleep duration, chronotype, insomnia, snoring, and daytime sleepiness, and were classified into healthy, intermediate, and poor. Having a poor compared to a healthy sleep pattern was related to significantly higher organ-specific age gaps for all but one organ (specifically pulmonary, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic, and brain), and was associated with faster pulmonary (OR 1.251, 95%CI: 1.116-1.404), hepatic (OR 1.382, 95%CI: 1.235-1.546), musculoskeletal (OR 1.708, 95%CI: 1.491-1.957), immune (OR 1.428, 95%CI: 1.292-1.579), metabolic (OR 1.659, 95%CI: 1.477-1.864), and brain (OR 1.592, 95%CI: 1.132-2.240) aging, as well as related to significantly higher likelihood of accelerated aging in multiple (≥ 2) organ systems (OR 1.463, 95%CI: 1.281-1.670). These findings demonstrate that poor sleep pattern is associated with accelerated pulmonary, hepatic, musculoskeletal, immune, metabolic and brain aging, highlighting sleep health as a modifiable target for delaying biological aging.

papers.title: GATA2-mediated IER3 transcription promotes breast cancer progression and tumor-associated immunosuppression.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhao Q, Li D, Li Y, Jinsihan D.
papers.abstract: The molecular mechanisms linking breast cancer (BC) progression to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment remain incompletely understood. We investigated the role of the GATA2/IER3 axis in BC progression and immune-related cellular responses. Bulk transcriptomic datasets GSE10810 and GSE42568 and the single-cell RNA sequencing dataset GSE161529 were integrated with immune-related gene lists. Support vector machine-recursive feature elimination, The Cancer Genome Atlas data, and immune-infiltration analyses prioritized candidate genes. Expression was evaluated in BC tissues and cell lines. Knockdown and rescue experiments assessed BC cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, and invasion, together with CD8+ T-cell responses and macrophage markers in coculture. Chromatin immunoprecipitation-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays examined transcriptional regulation, and nude mouse xenografts assessed tumor growth. Immediate early response 3 (IER3) was upregulated in BC tissues and cells and was associated with an immunosuppressive infiltration profile. IER3 knockdown inhibited BC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and increased apoptosis. It also enhanced CD8+ T-cell proliferation and interferon-γ secretion, reduced T-cell apoptosis, and decreased the proportion of CD206-positive macrophages. GATA binding protein 2 (GATA2) bound to the IER3 promoter and activated transcription. IER3 overexpression partially reversed the effects of GATA2 knockdown on BC cells and cocultured immune cells. In vivo, GATA2 knockdown reduced tumor growth, increased CD86 staining, and decreased CD206 staining; IER3 overexpression partially attenuated these effects (all p < 0.05). These findings support a role for GATA2-mediated IER3 transcription in BC progression and immune-related cellular responses. Its effects on adaptive antitumor immunity in vivo require further investigation.

papers.title: Glutamine Metabolism and Ferroptosis-related Gene Analysis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Prognosis and Immune Profiling.
papers.authors: Hu S, Yang F, Liu J, Liu H, Gao B, Liu Y, Cui C, Bai X, Zhang J, Yang X, Li B.
papers.abstract: Introduction Glutamine metabolism plays an essential role in the proliferation of hepatocellular carcinoma cells and the activation of immune cells to exert tumor- specific immunity. Ferroptosis inhibits the growth, proliferation and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma cells through various induction mechanisms, key enzymes and signaling pathways. This study aims to investigate the combined role of glutamine metabolism and ferroptosis-related genes (GFRG) in HCC prognosis and treatment response. Methods We identified synergistically expressed GFRG in 363 HCC patients from the TCGA cohort, using three machine learning methods and COX regression to develop a risk score. Patients from the TCGA and ICGC cohorts were divided into high and low GFRG score groups. We performed survival, immunoinfiltration, and drug sensitivity analyses to assess prognosis, immune profiles, and drug responses between the subtypes. Single-cell transcriptome sequencing quantified GFRG expression in tumor cells, while GFRG risk scores were analyzed in the tumor immune microenvironment to investigate risk subpopulation mechanisms. We validated key protein expressions using the Human Protein Atlas (HPA). Results Using machine learning, we identified four GFRGs and developed a risk model. High-risk patients exhibited poorer outcomes across training and validation cohorts, with higher immunosuppressive molecule expression and P53 mutations. They also showed increased resistance to drugs like sorafenib but were more responsive to immunotherapy. Pathway enrichment analysis revealed that numerous pathways implicated in tumor development were overexpressed in different risk subgroups. Our findings highlight immune and metabolic differences in HCC subpopulations based on GFRG scores, offering insights into HCC pathogenesis and treatment strategies. Discussion The results emphasize the prognostic significance of integrating glutamine metabolism and ferroptosis-related gene expression profiles in HCC. The association between high GFRG scores, immunosuppressive microenvironments, and differential drug responses suggests potential mechanisms driving tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. These insights align with existing literature on metabolic reprogramming and ferroptosis in cancer biology but also highlight the complexity of immune interactions in HCC. Limitations include reliance on retrospective cohorts and the need for functional validation in experimental models. Conclusion The GFRG scoring system is a crucial prognostic tool for HCC patients. High scores correlate with poor prognosis and increased immunosuppressive molecules, potentially enhancing immunotherapy response. The score independently predicts outcomes in both training and validation cohorts with strong predictive accuracy. Thus, GFRG can guide treatment decisions for HCC patients.

papers.title: Exploratory Analysis of MUC1 Expression and Prognostic Associations in Osteosarcoma.
papers.authors: Wang J, Han Y, Zhang G, Chen H, Yao Q.
papers.abstract: Background This study investigated MUC1 expression and its prognostic associations in Osteosarcoma (OS) using ferroptosis- and necroptosis-related transcriptional signatures to guide candidate gene selection. Methods Data from TARGET-OS, GSE218035, and GSE162454 were analyzed using single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (ssGSEA), weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), survival analysis, immune deconvolution, and virtual knockout analysis. MUC1 expression and cellular readouts following MUC1 knockdown were examined in U2OS cells, and a dual-luciferase reporter assay was performed to assess the interaction between miR-155-5p and the tested MUC1 sequence. Results Ferroptosis- and necroptosis-related transcriptional scores were positively correlated (r = 0.62). Among the three candidate genes, MUC1 was prioritized based on its highest module membership (0.519) and gene significance (0.201). Higher MUC1 expression in tumor tissues and its association with poorer survival were observed in the respective cohorts. MUC1 expression was associated with metabolic pathway scores and computationally inferred immune-cell composition. Virtual knockout predicted perturbations in phospholipid-related processes. In contrast to the tissue-level comparison, MUC1 mRNA expression was lower in U2OS cells than in hFOB1.19 cells. MUC1 knockdown was associated with increased CCK-8 signals and EdU-positive cell counts. The dual-luciferase reporter assay supported an interaction between miR-155-5p and the tested MUC1 sequence. Discussion Tissue-level and cell-line comparisons involved different biological systems and reference groups. Therefore, the U2OS findings should be interpreted within the specific experimental context. The computational analyses generated hypotheses but did not establish direct effects on ferroptosis, necroptosis, or immune-cell infiltration. Conclusion MUC1 expression was associated with prognosis and transcriptional features in the analyzed OS cohorts. However, its direct effects on ferroptosis, necroptosis, and immune cell infiltration remain to be established.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling reveals sex-specific microglial responses to simulated galactic cosmic radiation without broad inflammatory activation.
papers.authors: Osabutey MA, Calcines-Rodríguez L, Trojanczyk LA, Olschowka JA, O'Banion MK.
papers.abstract: Long‑duration deep space missions expose astronauts to galactic cosmic radiation (GCR), a complex mixture of high‑ and low‑LET ions that can compromise central nervous system (CNS) health. Microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, are highly sensitive to radiation, yet their cell‑state adaptations to space‑relevant mixed‑field exposure remain poorly defined. Here, we performed single‑cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of hippocampal and cortical microglia isolated from male and female C57BL/6 J mice 53 days after acute 100 cGy 5‑ion simulated GCR (GCRsim). Behavioral testing showed no overt deficits, but scRNA‑seq revealed subtle, sex‑specific transcriptional remodeling. Male microglia engaged a stress‑adaptive program characterized by upregulation of Fkbp5 , Ddit4 , Adrb1 , and metabolic regulators, with concurrent downregulation of ER chaperone genes. Female microglia displayed a transcriptionally blunted phenotype with selective induction of Fkbp5 , Ccnd3 , Tsc22d3 and Tnfaip2 , and broad downregulation of inflammatory and Nucleotide-binding Oligomerization Domain (NOD)/Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) pathways. Notably, canonical inflammatory or disease‑associated microglia (DAM) signatures were absent, and homeostatic markers ( P2ry12 , Cx3cr1 ) were preserved. FKBP5 immunoreactivity within Iba1 + microglia was significantly increased in both the dentate gyrus and cortex after GCRsim, without any change in total microglial volume. These findings define a non‑inflammatory, sex‑specific microglial response to space‑relevant GCR. This refined understanding of microglial adaptation provides a cellular framework for sex‑informed CNS risk assessment and countermeasure development for deep space travel.

papers.title: Integrating Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analysis Identifies FOSB as a Biomarker in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Dang LL, Zhang DL, Zhang Y, Zhou J, Zhang CS.
papers.abstract: Introduction Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) represents a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally, yet reliable biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain insufficient. IL-1 family signaling pathways are closely implicated in HCC initiation and progression, but integrated multi-omics analyses linking these pathways to practical biomarkers are lacking. In this study, we screened diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for HCC starting from a set of candidates associated with IL-1 family signaling pathways. Methods We retrieved bulk RNA-seq data from TCGA-LIHC and GEO databases, single-cell RNA-seq datasets from GEO, and IL-1 family signaling pathway-related gene sets from GeneCards. Differentially expressed gene screening, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and USet intersection analysis were applied to prioritize candidate genes; receiver operating characteristic curve, Kaplan-Meier survival, and multi-database validation were used to refine hub genes. We further constructed a prognostic risk score and nomogram, predicted upstream transcription factors, assessed immune infiltration and drug sensitivity, and delineated cell-specific expression, pseudotemporal expression patterns, and cell-cell communication patterns at single-cell level. Results Through multi-step screening, FOSB was identified as the key hub gene significantly downregulated in HCC tissues; at single-cell resolution, non-malignant cell populations exhibit high FOSB expression, whereas malignant tumor cell subsets exhibit low FOSB expression; high FOSB expression predicted favorable overall survival. CREB1 was predicted as the potential upstream transcription factor of FOSB. FOSB expression was closely correlated with immune cell infiltration, tumor angiogenesis signatures and in silico predicted sensitivity to two non-standard compounds. GSEA suggested FOSB may be involved in PPAR pathway-related signatures; pseudotime and cell-cell communication analyses revealed associations of FOSB with tumor cell trajectory dynamics and intercellular crosstalk, which represent testable hypotheses for future mechanistic investigation. Conclusions This study identifies FOSB as a potential biomarker for HCC via multi-cohort transcriptomic and single-cell analysis, links it to IL-1 family signaling-related signatures, immune infiltration, angiogenesis-related molecular signatures, and predicted drug sensitivity, and provides computational clues for HCC diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and future targeted-therapy-oriented research.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Convergent and Divergent Macrophage Polarization in Myocardial Infarction and Takotsubo Syndrome.
papers.authors: Li B, Bao Y, Pei H, Yang F, Qu X, Yin D.
papers.abstract: Objective To compare, at the transcriptomic level, the infiltration characteristics and transcriptional differences of cardiac macrophages at 24 h after modeling between myocardial infarction (MI) and Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). Methods Bulk RNA-seq data obtained 1 h and 24 h after modeling, and single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data obtained 24 h after modeling, from mouse models of MI and TTS were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis and pathway enrichment analysis were performed on the bulk RNA-seq data, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify hub genes. scRNA-seq data were used for macrophage re-clustering, integrative comparison and hdWGCNA analysis. Protein expression was assessed by Western blotting and immunofluorescence in MI and TTS rat models. Results Bulk RNA sequencing revealed that MI was characterized predominantly by neutrophil chemotaxis and inflammatory cascades in the early phase, whereas TTS displayed type I interferon responses and antiviral-like immune transcriptional features. PPI network analysis identified that the hub genes in MI were enriched for AP-1 transcription factors and pro-inflammatory cytokines, while those in TTS were almost exclusively interferon-stimulated genes. Single-cell sequencing showed that both neutrophils and macrophages infiltrated the myocardium in MI and TTS, with neutrophils predominating in MI and macrophages in TTS; integrated analysis further showed that MI associated macrophages exhibited pro-fibrotic transcriptional features, whereas TTS associated macrophages displayed pro-inflammatory and oxidative stress transcriptional features. hdWGCNA identified tissue remodeling modules in MI and pro-inflammatory modules in TTS, and highlighted upregulation of Ifih1 and Ccrl2 in TTS and of S100a9 in MI. Conclusion At 24 h after modeling, MI associated macrophages displayed pro-fibrotic transcriptional features, whereas TTS associated macrophages displayed stress and inflammation related transcriptional features. These transcriptional differences may be related to the divergent ventricular remodeling that follows in each disease. Ccrl2 and Ifih1 in TTS and S100a9 in MI are candidate genes warranting further functional validation.

papers.title: Insights on Intestinal Fibrosis: From Stromal Cell Heterogeneity and Metabolic Reprogramming to Novel Therapeutic Strategies.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Wang J, Xu R, Bai X, Zhang Y, Bi X.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of inflammatory bowel disease, and it can lead to fixed strictures, intestinal obstruction, and repeated surgical intervention. Although effective control of inflammation may limit ongoing tissue injury, no approved therapy selectively prevents or reverses established intestinal fibrosis. This therapeutic gap reflects an incomplete understanding of the cellular and metabolic mechanisms that sustain fibrotic remodeling. In this review, we integrate classical extracellular-matrix pathways with recent single-cell, spatial, and metabolic evidence to provide a multicellular framework for intestinal fibrogenesis. Single-cell studies indicate that intestinal fibroblasts comprise overlapping and environmentally responsive states rather than fixed lineages. Their activation is shaped by reciprocal communication with immune cells, epithelial and endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, creeping fat, and the intestinal microbiota. Metabolic reprogramming provides an additional layer of regulation through glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway, glutamine-proline metabolism, lactate-associated signaling, and extracellular metabolite sensing. However, the strength of evidence varies among these mechanisms, and direct links between defined fibroblast states and specific metabolic dependencies remain limited. In this review, we further discuss therapeutic opportunities targeting immune-stromal communication, pathogenic fibroblast programs, cellular metabolism, extracellular-matrix turnover, and mechanotransduction. Translating these opportunities into stage-specific interventions will require spatially resolved functional models to validate causal targets and fibrosis-selective biomarkers to assess therapeutic effects.

papers.title: ETS1 as a Candidate Biomarker for Sepsis‑Associated Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome: Multi‑Omics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
papers.authors: Leng L, Deng Y, Tian Y.
papers.abstract: Objective This multi‑omics study aimed to screen candidate molecules associated with the transition from sepsis to sepsis‑associated ARDS, and provide preliminary biological evidence for risk‑stratification research. Methods Public transcriptomic datasets were used for differential‑gene analysis, WGCNA, lung‑tissue‑expression filtering and multi‑algorithm machine‑learning screening. We performed transcriptome sequencing on peripheral blood samples from our exploratory single‑center cohort including 22 sepsis patients and 10 healthy volunteers to verify gene dysregulation in sepsis vs healthy status. Associations between gene expression and established ARDS among sepsis patients were assessed using the public dataset GSE32707 only. Single‑cell RNA‑seq data, functional enrichment and literature mining were applied to explore potential molecular mechanisms. Results Twenty‑seven candidate genes related to septic lung injury were obtained. ETS1 emerged as a hub gene with high model contribution across machine‑learning and SHAP interpretability analyses. In our clinical cohort, ETS1 was significantly down‑regulated in sepsis patients compared with healthy controls. Analysis of the public GSE32707 dataset further suggested that ETS1 exhibited stepwise reduction from healthy controls, through uncomplicated sepsis, to sepsis complicated with ARDS. Single‑cell analysis demonstrated that ETS1 was predominantly expressed in NK cells, T cells and B‑cells, implying potential roles in immune‑homeostasis regulation. Our machine‑learning models achieved high classification performance for discriminating sepsis from healthy volunteers. However, this classification task cannot directly predict incident ARDS among sepsis patients. Conclusion In this hypothesis‑generating observational multi‑omics study, reduced ETS1 expression was correlated with sepsis and further decreased in patients with established sepsis‑associated ARDS in one public dataset. ETS1 represents a candidate correlative biomarker for sepsis risk stratification. Further large multi‑center cohorts, cell‑composition correction and functional wet‑lab experiments are required to validate whether ETS1 can support ARDS early‑warning or serve as a therapeutic target for septic lung injury.

papers.title: Integrative blood transcriptomic analysis identifies IFIT3 as a candidate biomarker associated with host immune responses in tuberculosis.
papers.authors: Kaisaier A, Alim A, Xie J, Yang H, Reyimu A, Liu W, Xu A.
papers.abstract: Background Blood-based host-response biomarkers may complement pathogen-directed tests for tuberculosis (TB). We integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses with clinical validation to identify immune-related blood biomarkers, focusing on interferon-induced protein with tetratricopeptide repeats 3 (IFIT3). Methods Four peripheral-blood microarray datasets (GSE42834, GSE83456, GSE19491, and GSE19439) were analyzed using GEO2R. Differentially expressed genes were evaluated by protein-protein interaction analysis, functional enrichment, immune-cell deconvolution, and gene set enrichment analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were used to characterize candidate-gene expression across immune-cell populations. IFIT3 expression was assessed by RT-qPCR in a small independent cohort of 10 patients with TB and 11 healthy controls. Results The analysis identified 96 shared differentially expressed genes and eight key interferon-related genes: STAT1, IFIT3, IFI44, OAS2, IFIT2, RSAD2, XAF1, and OAS1. TB samples showed lower estimated proportions of CD8+ T cells and resting CD4+ memory T cells and higher proportions of monocytes, activated dendritic cells, and neutrophils. Across the available human PBMC single-cell data, IFIT3 was detected across several innate and adaptive immune-cell populations. In the small independent cohort, RT-qPCR showed higher IFIT3 expression in TB samples, with a preliminary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.763. Conclusions IFIT3 is a candidate blood-based host-response biomarker associated with TB-related immune responses, while its clinical utility remains to be established in larger prospective cohorts and clinically relevant control groups.

papers.title: Computational Prediction of Elbasvir as a Theoretical Candidate for PFOS-Associated Gut and Skin Shared Pathologies.
papers.authors: Du Y, Chen X, Lv Y, Zhong J.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) frequently co-occur along the gut-skin axis, yet the systemic triggers, particularly environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals like perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate network toxicology and single-cell multi-omics to propose a computational framework for the shared molecular signatures of PFOS-driven AD and IBD comorbidity. Utilizing large-scale clinical transcriptomic cohorts and machine learning, we computationally predicted the transcription factor MYC as a potential core pathological hub. Single-cell transcriptomics and in silico virtual perturbation models revealed that aberrant MYC activation is highly restricted to barrier-forming cells: epidermal keratinocytes and intestinal mucosal progenitors. This spatially specific dysregulation not only compromises epithelial structural integrity but also reshapes local chemotactic networks, driving macrophage pro-inflammatory polarization and immune imbalance. To translate these findings, high-throughput drug repurposing screening and 200 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations identified the antiviral drug Elbasvir as a stable, high-affinity MYC inhibitor. Collectively, our work proposes a single-cell spatial pathology of environment-driven shared pathologies across the gut-skin axis and provides a theoretical pharmacological strategy to intervene in systemic inflammatory networks.

papers.title: In Vitro Directed Evolution of Antibodies as Molecular Recognition Elements for Advanced Biosensors: Strategies, Mechanisms, and Applications.
papers.authors: Zhang R, Wang J, Chen M, Shu H, Liu H, Yang H.
papers.abstract: Antibodies are widely used as molecular recognition elements in biosensors because of their high affinity, specificity, and versatility. However, their performance may require further optimization when detecting low-abundance targets, structurally related compounds, or analytes in complex sample matrices. In recent years, in vitro directed evolution has provided a complementary approach to antibody engineering by enabling controlled sequence diversification and selection under application-relevant conditions. This review summarizes recent advances in the in vitro directed evolution of antibodies for biosensing applications. Major engineering strategies are discussed, including random diversification and recombination, semi-rational and focused mutagenesis, structure- and sequence-based design, and AI-assisted optimization. The influence of antibody formats, including full-length antibodies, Fab fragments, single-chain variable fragments (scFvs), and nanobodies, on library construction, selection, and molecular recognition is also examined. Furthermore, strategies for evolving antibodies against small molecules, peptides, and protein antigens are reviewed, highlighting how antigen properties influence the design of diversification and selection approaches. Representative applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, and biomedical diagnosis are evaluated, with attention to antibody-level improvements and their translation into biosensor performance. Finally, current limitations and future opportunities are discussed, particularly in relation to screening efficiency, reproducibility, application-oriented evaluation, and the integration of computational methods and advanced biosensing platforms.

papers.title: ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D Are associated with urea cycle activity and ammonia stress responses in prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Huang L, Jiang S, Zeng G, Gao J, Shan H, Huang K.
papers.abstract: Background Prostate cancer (PRAD) progression is closely associated with metabolic reprogramming, but the role of nitrogen metabolism and ammonia-associated cell death remains unclear. This study investigates the clinical and functional significance of urea cycle activity in PRAD. Methods Transcriptomic data from TCGA-PRAD and single-cell RNA-seq dataset GSE221603 were analyzed. ssGSEA was used to quantify urea cycle activity. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, survival analysis, and multiple machine learning algorithms were applied to identify key genes. Immune infiltration, pathway enrichment, and single-cell functional analyses were performed. Experimental validation was conducted using siRNA knockdown, qPCR, Western blot, CCK-8, apoptosis assays, and NH4Cl-induced ammonia stress models. Results Higher urea cycle scores were associated with longer progression-free survival, although the association with progression-free survival was not significant after adjustment for StromalScore or tumor purity. Urea cycle scores were associated with distinct immune infiltration patterns and metabolic pathway reprogramming. Multi-algorithm integration identified ADRA1D and PGM5 as candidate genes associated with the urea cycle phenotype, with single-cell analyses revealing differences in their expression across cellular populations. A putative ADAMTS9-AS1/miR-183-3p/ADRA1D regulatory axis was identified and associated with urea cycle activity and cellular responses to ammonia-associated stress. ADAMTS9-AS1 knockdown reduced ADRA1D expression, decreased intracellular arginine levels, and enhanced cellular sensitivity to NH₄Cl-associated stress. Conclusion Urea cycle activity is associated with a favorable metabolic phenotype in PRAD and may contribute to cellular adaptation to ammonia stress. ADAMTS9-AS1 and ADRA1D may represent candidate genes associated with this metabolic network, providing potential targets for further investigation of nitrogen metabolism in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Pathogenesis and immune responses to Eurasian avian-like H1N1 and influenza D virus in pigs.
papers.authors: Vats A, Yang L, Sedaghat-Rostami E, Hatton C, Briggs E, Freimanis G, Downing T, van Reeth K, Paudyal B, Salguero FJ, Gerner W, Tchilian E.
papers.abstract: Introduction Eurasian avian-like H1N1 (EAavH1N1) and influenza D viruses (IDV), with their ongoing evolution and zoonotic potential, are a serious threat to animal and human health. Using experimental infection of pigs, we characterized and compared their pathogenesis and immune responses. Methods Pigs were infected intranasally with either IDV or EAavH1N1. We evaluated viral replication kinetics, respiratory tract pathology, local and systemic antibody and cellular immune responses, and conducted lung single-cell transcriptomics to assess changes at early and later infection stages. Results EAavH1N1 induced rapid viral clearance and early immune activation, including robust systemic and mucosal antibody responses and increased IFNγ and TNF production. This heightened immune response was associated with more severe pathology of the upper and lower respiratory tract. In contrast, IDV infection resulted in prolonged viral shedding and higher viral titres, with delayed and attenuated cellular immune responses. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of lungs further indicated early and persistent suppression of antiviral and innate immune pathways during IDV infection. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that EAavH1N1 and IDV exhibit distinct viral kinetics, immune activation profiles, and lung responses, providing insight into differences in transmission dynamics, disease severity, and immune control among influenza virus types in swine.

papers.title: Cohort-aware single-cell analysis of PBMCs identifies an interferon program specific to primary Sjögren's syndrome and limited immune convergence with periodontitis.
papers.authors: Qin T, Sun C, Sun J, Zhang A, Zhang X, Chen L, Zhou Q.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) are epidemiologically linked, and shared peripheral immune dysregulation has been proposed. Published comparisons rest on bulk transcriptomes or on tests that treat cells as replicates, and in public data disease is confounded with study. We reanalyzed four public single-cell RNA-seq cohorts of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs; two PD, two pSS) with the donor as the unit of inference and cases compared with same-cohort controls. After removal of eight duplicated samples, 48 donors (24 controls, 10 PD, 14 pSS) and 317,205 cells in 28 subsets were analyzed for composition, pseudobulk expression and consensus regulon activity. A finding was considered replicated when significant in the pooled model (false discovery rate + T cells were reduced in both pSS cohorts. Cross-disease concordance was weak but exceeded permutation nulls (regulons, rho = 0.38, P = 0.031; genes, rho = 0.13, P = 0.012) and had two components: fewer CD56dim NK cells and more cells of a mixed T-like/adaptive-like NK subset in all four cohorts, and lower expression of glucocorticoid- and stress-responsive genes in cases across lineages. With pooled controls, the same data yielded "shared" regulons that did not survive cohort-aware testing, and 39%-68% of regulon-subset pairs differed between the controls of the PD and pSS studies. The replicated peripheral immune change is specific to pSS; what the two diseases share is limited to a compositional shift in the NK lineage and a stress-response signature of uncertain origin.

papers.title: Tandem TRA/TRD loci expand TCRα/δ recombination topology in crocodilians.
papers.authors: Li Q, Qin H, Jin Y, Qiu Z, Xiao S, Mu L, Wu G, Tian S, Pan X, Yao X, Li J, Ma L.
papers.abstract: Crocodilians retain an unusual tandem organization of two classical TRA/TRD composite loci, but whether this architecture alters receptor recombination has been unclear. Here, chromosome-level annotation of Chinese alligator ( Alligator sinensis ) and American alligator ( Alligator mississippiensis ) TR loci, integrated with recombination signal sequence (RSS) analysis and RNA-seq-derived repertoire reconstruction, shows that both TRA/TRD modules are transcriptionally productive and functionally connected. In Alligator sinensis , 30.6% of classified TRA rearrangements joined a V segment from one module to a J segment in the other. For TRD , 33.0% followed a cross-locus V-D route followed by local D-J joining. RSS orientation supports deletional recombination across the co-oriented tandem loci, whereas C-region association remains local through RNA splicing. These findings identify spatial connectivity between duplicated antigen-receptor modules as an additional layer of TCR diversity generation in crocodilians.
